faq.q: How much does it cost to install video surveillance?
faq.a: The cost depends on the number of cameras, equipment type, and installation complexity. We conduct free site surveys, prepare estimates, and provide commercial proposals.

faq.q: What is the difference between IP cameras and analog cameras?
faq.a: IP cameras offer higher resolution, video analytics, and flexible network scaling; analog cameras (HDCVI/TVI) are more affordable and work over coaxial cable. We select the right solution based on your budget and requirements.

faq.q: Can I view cameras from my phone?
faq.a: Yes, we set up remote access from your phone and computer, as well as cloud viewing and notifications.

faq.q: How long is the recording archive stored?
faq.a: Archive depth depends on storage capacity, number of cameras, and resolution — typically 7 to 30 days. We calculate the retention period based on your specific needs.

faq.q: Do you service the system after installation?
faq.a: Yes, we provide warranty and maintenance services, dispatch technicians for diagnostics and repairs throughout Uzbekistan.

faq.q: What makes an IP intercom better than an analog one?
faq.a: IP intercoms deliver high-quality video, remote viewing from your phone from anywhere, recording capability, and seamless integration with smart home systems and access control.

faq.q: Can I answer calls from my phone?
faq.a: Absolutely. When someone calls from the panel, the call comes to your smartphone — you can unlock the door remotely, even if you're away from home or the office.

faq.q: Is it suitable for multi-apartment buildings?
faq.a: Yes, we design multi-unit intercom systems for residential complexes complete with call panels and individual monitors in each unit.

faq.q: How much does intercom installation cost in Tashkent?
faq.a: For a flat or a private house the price is the kit (door station + monitor) plus installation: an analogue kit costs less, an IP video intercom with recording and smartphone unlock costs more. For an apartment entrance the price depends on the number of units. We usually send a quote the same day after a short call.

faq.q: Can the intercom be connected to an electronic lock and access control?
faq.a: Yes, that is a standard part of our projects: the intercom releases an electromagnetic or electromechanical lock, while residents and staff use cards, codes or fingerprints. For offices we merge the intercom with the access control system into one setup with a shared entry log.

faq.q: What distance can fiber optic cable cover?
faq.a: Single-mode fiber works for tens of kilometers without amplifiers, so connecting buildings, branches, and sites across the city has virtually no distance limitations.

faq.q: Do you provide fiber splicing services with on-site visits?
faq.a: Yes, we come out with a fusion splicer and optical time-domain reflectometer: we splice fibers, install distribution frames and couplers, and provide measurement reports for each line.

faq.q: Do you repair fiber optic breaks?
faq.a: Yes, we locate the damage point using an OTDR and restore the line—either by on-site splicing or replacing the damaged section.

faq.q: What does integration add over separate systems?
faq.a: Events stop being orphans: an alarm pulls up the right camera, a card pass is recorded with video, a fire signal releases doors and starts the announcement. The operator gets one screen instead of five applications.

faq.q: Can different installed brands be combined?
faq.a: Usually yes: open protocols (ONVIF, OSDP, Modbus, vendor APIs) link equipment from different makers. After an audit we say honestly what integrates as is and what is cheaper to replace.

faq.q: Do you link access control to time attendance and 1C?
faq.a: Yes, a standard task: passes flow into timesheets and 1C, lateness and overtime are computed automatically.

faq.q: What about resilience?
faq.a: Critical services run on a virtualised, redundant server platform (H3C); power is protected by UPS, archives by RAID. A unified system does not mean a single point of failure.

calc.lead: Tick the systems your site needs — the calculator lays out a plan, counts the points and metres of cable routes and shows the labour cost from our standard price list. Below are worked examples for typical sites and the unit rates behind them. It takes a minute and commits you to nothing.

faq.q: How accurate is the calculator?
faq.a: It is a guide based on our standard price list for installation work: it shows the range a site with these parameters usually falls into. A firm quote follows a site visit, where the engineer checks the layout, the state of the routes and the ceiling height.

faq.q: Does the figure include equipment?
faq.a: No. The calculator prices the work only: mounting, cable laying, termination and commissioning. Cameras, recorders, controllers and detectors can be bought from our catalogue or supplied by you — it does not change the installation price.

faq.q: Is the site visit chargeable?
faq.a: No, the survey visit within Tashkent is free. The engineer comes at a time that suits you, takes measurements and confirms where the routes will run.

faq.q: Why a range instead of a single figure?
faq.a: The range covers what cannot be seen remotely: the real length of the routes, wall construction, whether concrete has to be chased, and how hard access is. The lower bound is a straightforward site, the upper one carries a margin.

faq.q: Do you work with companies under contract?
faq.a: Yes. We work under contract with completion certificates and a warranty, accept bank transfer and issue invoices. For larger projects we produce a full design and specification.

faq.q: What does CCTV cost for a private house?
faq.a: A 250 m² house with six cameras and a video door entry runs about 3.6–4.5 million UZS for the labour. Most of that is not the cameras but the cable routes: in a house the cable runs around the perimeter and out to the gate. With ducts already in place the work is roughly a quarter cheaper.

faq.q: How much is installing one camera?
faq.a: An indoor camera starts at 155,000 UZS, an outdoor one at 180,000, a PTZ at 310,000. On top of that come the point setup, commissioning and the cable run to the recorder. A single camera on its own is subject to our minimum order of 560,000 UZS.

faq.q: What is the cable laying price per metre?
faq.a: Surface laying starts at 7,000 UZS per metre, pulling into an existing tray or conduit at 5,500. Where no routes exist, conduit and chasing are added — and we price those by route length, not per cable, so a bundle of ten cables does not cost ten times more.
